titles.title: SeriousSamFirstEncounter
titles.engine: Croteam Serious Engine 1, retail v1.00. Bin\SeriousSam.exe is 425,984 B and Bin\Engine.dll is 1,560,576 B (md5 6281c69ec427b9a0dd828bc1cbf0b14b); both were linked 2001-02-28. The engine log prints 'Serious Sam version: v1.00'. The renderer is OpenGL only: Engine.dll names OPENGL32.DLL and contains no D3D8 or Direct3DCreate8 string.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 fullscreen OpenGL on the XP LCD boxes. Scripts\Game_startup.ini carries 'sam_bFullScreen=1; sam_iScreenSizeI=<W>; sam_iScreenSizeJ=<H>; gfx_iRefreshRate=<Hz>;'. All three launchers write it after 'call FLEETRES.BAT' (lines 54-61 of 'Play Serious Sam - The First Encounter.bat'), and the GAMERES 'ssam' GR_OP_CFG rule in agent/shared/gameres.h writes it at sync. The engine includes PersistentSymbols.ini first and Game_startup.ini second, and CDS_SetMode does not check the menu table, so any mode the driver offers is set. The mechanism is present and correct for v1.00; gfx_iRefreshRate is TFE 1.00's real cvar. The deployed Game_startup.ini on .123, .145, .195 and .240 reads 1920/1080/60 with the header 'written by GAMESYNC'. The .240 engine log confirms it: 'Starting display mode: 1920x1080xDesktop ICD fullscreen', 'CDS: mode set to 1920x1080x0', 'OpenGL context created: ... RADEON X800'. Exception: on .195 (Windows 7, Radeon HD 5450) TFE 1.00 cannot set any mode. Its log shows 'CDS error: DISP_CHANGE_BADMODE' for 1920x1080 and for all four 640x480 recovery modes, then 'FatalError: Cannot set display mode!'. The title does not run on that box at all; the compat DB already marks it +X.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded table in Engine.dll (_areResolutions[], file offset 0x159200, 22 int32 w,h pairs): 320x240 400x300 480x360 512x384 640x480 720x540 800x600 960x720 1024x768 1152x864 1280x960 1280x1024 1600x1200 1792x1344 1856x1392 1920x1440 2048x1536 1280x480 1600x600 2048x768 848x480 856x480. An entry is kept only if ChangeDisplaySettings(CDS_TEST|CDS_FULLSCREEN) accepts it; the table has a single code xref at 0x600fad9a, the OpenGL loop. The fullscreen RESOLUTION trigger under Video Options shows only this filtered list, so on these 1080p panels it tops out at 1280x1024 / 1280x960. 1600x1200 is not offered by these panels. The windowed list in SeriousSam.exe (file offset 0x2fb14, 320x240..2048x1536) has no 1920x1080 either. Because 1920x1080 is missing, the menu shows 640x480 as the current value (the SizeToResolution fallback) while the game actually runs at 1920x1080. Applying any video change from that screen would therefore set 640x480 until the next launch.
titles.evidence: All paths below are under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/. static-serious-engine-tables.txt holds the table dump, the xref and the refresh cvar names. The per-box files {123,145,195,240}/SeriousSamFirstEncounter__Scripts_Game_startup.ini show 1920/1080/60 on every LCD box. 195/SeriousSamFirstEncounter__SeriousSam.log shows BADMODE for every mode and the FatalError. 240/SeriousSamFirstEncounter__SeriousSam.log shows the mode set to 1920x1080. {box}/gameres.json shows EDID LCD panels, persisted 1920x1080, and driver lists ending in 1920x1080@60. SeriousSam.exe carries the menu strings 'ETRSVIDEO OPTIONS', 'ETRSRESOLUTION' and 'ETRSAPPLY'. The menu logic comes from the GPL Serious Engine 1.10 source (web, github.com/Croteam-official/Serious-Engine): FillResolutionsList calls _pGfx->EnumDisplayModes, SizeToResolution falls back to 640x480, and Adapter.cpp says 'enumerate modes thru resolution list'. The retail table is identical to that source apart from 720x576, which is not in TFE 1.00.
titles.fix: Patch the table data in the staged Bin\Engine.dll. Overwrite the three 8:3 Matrox dual-head entries, which are useless on a single monitor, with little-endian int32 pairs: 0x159288 (1280,480) becomes 1280,720; 0x159290 (1600,600) becomes 1600,900; 0x159298 (2048,768) becomes 1920,1080. Replace entries rather than append, because the entry count is a compiled loop bound. The new entries render as ordinary modes: IsDualHead() is exactly 8:3 and IsWideScreen() matches only 856x480. The file size stays the same. After the patch the RESOLUTION list offers 1920x1080 and pre-selects it. Separately for .195: TFE 1.00 has no working display path on Win7. The TFE 1.05 patch on the share contains the 1.05 engine, with D3D8 and the CDS code that works for TSE 1.05 on that same box. Its Engine.dll holds the same table at base 0x1ad6c0 and would need the same three-entry edit.
titles.fix_source: The table edit is already in tree: an in-place binary edit of /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/SeriousSamFirstEncounter/Bin/Engine.dll, with nothing to download. Optional for .195: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Game Updates/serious-sam-tfe-1.05.zip contains SeriousSamPatch105_Euro.exe (94 files). Its Engine.dll (md5 c06964beff031be8773536957685d874) names D3D8.DLL and gap_iRefreshRate, and its SeriousSam.exe carries no stxt, BoG_ or secdrv.
titles.fix_risk: Low for the table edit. Only the menu enumeration reads the table, from one code site, and the runtime mode set is unchanged. The game already runs at 1920x1080 through the launcher; Serious Engine 1 keeps a fixed horizontal FOV, so 16:9 is vert-, as it is today. Multiplayer should be unaffected, because the table is not part of the network protocol and the host's ssam-tfe-server uses its own copy of DedicatedServer.exe and Engine.dll. That still has to be proven: join 192.168.1.132:25600 (v1.00) from a patched client, and run a two-box LAN game. Publishing: this edit keeps the file size, so write it through gvfs and verify the md5 through /mnt. smbclient stamps files on this NAS with Oct 2007, and GAMESYNC's size+mtime test would then skip the new file on every box. The TFE 1.05 upgrade is a bigger step: it breaks joins to the host's v1.00 TFE server unless that server is upgraded too, and it is the Euro build going onto a US tree (disc label SERIOUS_SAM_RC2).
titles.hw_check: Use .145 or .240 (both XP). XP's GDI can capture fullscreen OpenGL, and both boxes report disc_mount through d347bus. Do not use .195: TFE dies there, and Windows 7 cannot capture exclusive fullscreen. Launch with EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\SeriousSamFirstEncounter" "Play Serious Sam - The First Encounter.bat", wait about 40 s, then SCREENSHOT 0. The menu is keyboard-navigable (arrows, Enter, Esc); synthetic keys are known to reach this engine, as the .195 TSE log line '-> dem_bScreenShot=1;' shows. Use UIKEY DOWN/RETURN to reach OPTIONS > VIDEO OPTIONS, put the cursor on RESOLUTION, and press UIKEY LEFT/RIGHT, taking a SCREENSHOT for each value. Expected today: the value shows 640x480 and cycles only up to 1280x1024, with no 1920x1080. Expected after the patch: 1920x1080 is listed and pre-selected. Do not press APPLY. Leave with Esc, then DOWNLOAD C:\Games\SeriousSamFirstEncounter\SeriousSam.log and confirm the line 'Starting display mode: 1920x1080'. Close the game with taskkill /f /im "SeriousSam.exe".
titles.verifier_notes: (1) .195's hand-written per-box Scripts\PersistentSymbols.ini carries sam_iDriver=1. In TFE 1.00 that value selects adapter 1, the '3Dfx' standalone-OpenGL adapter; the log shows 'Starting display mode: 1920x1080xDesktop 3Dfx fullscreen'. It is not the root cause, because the ICD recovery modes fail with BADMODE as well, but it is wrong state and should be removed. (2) .123 now has DAEMON Tools (HWPROFILE disc_mount true via d347bus), and its All Users desktop shows all three Serious Sam shortcuts. The compat DB rows calling .123 'n/a' because the shortcuts are suppressed are therefore stale; see desktop-shortcuts.txt. (3) .240 is no longer in the state the task describes. At about 00:12 EDT on 2026-09-29 its GAMERES reported EDID DELL E2313H, an LCD, persisted and live 1920x1080, and 1920x1080@60 in the mode list. (4) stage-fleetres.py --check --dry-run against /mnt reports this title as current.

titles.title: SeriousSamSecondEncounter
titles.engine: Croteam Serious Engine 1, retail v1.05. Bin\Engine.dll is 1,929,274 B (md5 230c1b52f3bd125dc9af049b70472100) and Bin\SeriousSam.exe is 442,434 B; both were linked 2001-12-12, and the log prints 'v1.05'. It has both OpenGL and Direct3D 8 renderers. ModEXT.txt contains 'MP', which loads GameMP and EntitiesMP. TSE 1.07 must not be applied: NOTES.txt records that its exe is wrapped in SafeDisc 2.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 fullscreen, set the same way as TFE: all three launchers and the GAMERES 'ssam' rule write Scripts\Game_startup.ini. The engine logs confirm it on .195 ('Starting display mode: 1920x1080xdesktop (fullscreen)', 'CDS: mode set to 1920x1080x0', 'OpenGL context created ... AMD Radeon HD 5450') and on .240 (RADEON 9800 XT ICD at 1920x1080). The mechanism is present but DEFECTIVE in two ways. (a) Both writers replace the whole file. The launcher uses '> "%~dp0Scripts\Game_startup.ini"' and GAMERES uses GR_OP_CFG. The staged file is TSE's own 4-line script, which sets sam_strFirstLevel to Levels/LevelsMP/1_0_InTheLastEpisode.wld, sam_strIntroLevel to Levels/LevelsMP/Intro.wld, sam_strTechTestLevel, and sam_strGameName to 'serioussamse'. Without it, TSE's exe falls back to TFE defaults compiled into the binary: sam_strFirstLevel is bound to 0x442f7c, initialised to 'Levels\01_Hatshepsut.wld', and sam_strIntroLevel to 0x442f78, initialised to 'Levels\Intro.wld'. Neither level exists in the TSE tree. On all four LCD boxes the deployed file now holds only the 7 GAMESYNC lines. The .195 and .240 logs show the result: 'Cannot start game: Cannot open file `C:\Games\SeriousSamSecondEncounter\Levels\Intro.wld'' — the menu background level fails to load. A New Game would target the absent Hatshepsut level; that was not observed. (b) gfx_iRefreshRate is TFE's cvar name; TSE's is gap_iRefreshRate. The logs show 'Scripts\Game_startup.ini(7): Identifier 'gfx_iRefreshRate' is not declared' (line 8 in the older .240 run), so the refresh line never applies. That is harmless on these 60 Hz LCDs.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded table in Engine.dll at file offset 0x1ad6d0, 23 entries: 320x240 400x300 480x360 512x384 640x480 720x540 720x576 800x600 960x720 1024x768 1152x864 1280x960 1280x1024 1600x1200 1792x1344 1856x1392 1920x1440 2048x1536 1280x480 1600x600 2048x768 848x480 856x480. Both renderers walk this same table. The OpenGL loop at 0x6003a8a1 runs CDS_TEST over 0x601ad6d0..0x601ad788. The Direct3D loop at 0x6003ab16 calls IDirect3D8::EnumAdapterModes ([edx+0x1c]) and keeps a mode only if it equals a table entry with format 0x15-0x19 and passes CheckDeviceType ([edx+0x24]). Switching the DRIVER trigger to Direct3D therefore does not help. As with TFE, the RESOLUTION value falls back to showing 640x480, and applying from that screen would set it.
titles.evidence: All paths below are under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/. static-serious-engine-tables.txt holds the TSE table, both code loops, and the gap_ versus gfx_ refresh cvar. static-tse-level-defaults.txt holds the xrefs and static initialisers that bind the level symbols, the staged 224-byte Game_startup.ini, and a case-insensitive listing of the gro archives showing only Levels/LevelsMP/*.wld. {195,240}/SeriousSamSecondEncounter__SeriousSam.log show the Intro.wld failure and the undeclared gfx_iRefreshRate. {123,145,195,240}/SeriousSamSecondEncounter__Scripts_Game_startup.ini show the TSE lines gone. The GPL 1.10 source has the same table (web).
titles.fix: (1) For the menu, apply the same data-only table patch to the staged Engine.dll: 0x1ad760 (1280,480) becomes 1280,720; 0x1ad768 (1600,600) becomes 1600,900; 0x1ad770 (2048,768) becomes 1920,1080. OpenGL and Direct3D will then both list 1920x1080. (2) A must-fix that is independent of the menu: stop overwriting TSE's own startup script. The cleanest form mirrors id Tech 3's fleetres.cfg. Stage Game_startup.ini as its shipped 4 lines plus a last line include "Scripts\\FleetRes.ini"; — not yet tested. Then make both writers produce only Scripts\FleetRes.ini. The launcher block is ssam_startup_ini() in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py, embedded in provisioning/discmount/specs/SeriousSamSecondEncounter-{Play,Host,Join}.json and regenerated with make-mount-launcher.py. In agent/shared/gameres.h, add a TSE variant of the 'ssam' body that emits gap_iRefreshRate instead of gfx_iRefreshRate. The alternative is to re-emit the four TSE lines from both writers. Either way, update tests/python/test_gameres_mirror.py and the tests that pin the ssam block. (3) Do not use TSE 1.07. It adds SafeDisc 2, and the 1.10 source table has the same 23 entries, so it would not add 16:9.
titles.fix_source: Everything needed is in tree. The table edit targets /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/SeriousSamSecondEncounter/Bin/Engine.dll. The TSE startup lines come from the staged Scripts/Game_startup.ini itself. The code changes are in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py, provisioning/discmount/specs/SeriousSamSecondEncounter-*.json and agent/shared/gameres.h.
titles.fix_risk: The Engine.dll edit is low risk for the same reasons as TFE. Still prove a join to the host's ssam-tse-server (v1.05, port 25610) and a two-box LAN game, and publish through gvfs because the edit keeps the file size. The startup-script fix is also low risk, but it touches the shared discmount generator and gameres.h, which means an agent release and a fleet-wide GAMESYNC. The lost sam_strGameName may also affect TSE's LAN and Internet server browser, which is relevant to the favourites work; that effect is unverified.
titles.hw_check: Use .240 or .145. .195 renders but cannot be photographed in exclusive fullscreen. Launch with EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\SeriousSamSecondEncounter" "Play Serious Sam - The Second Encounter.bat", then use the keyboard: OPTIONS > VIDEO OPTIONS > RESOLUTION, stepping with LEFT/RIGHT. Check the list with the DRIVER trigger set to OpenGL and again set to Direct3D, taking a SCREENSHOT for each value. Expected today: the list opens at 640x480 and tops out at 1280x1024. Expected after the patch: 1920x1080 is present. Also start SINGLE PLAYER > NEW GAME and confirm the first level loads rather than failing with 'Cannot open file ... Levels\01_Hatshepsut.wld'. Then DOWNLOAD C:\Games\SeriousSamSecondEncounter\SeriousSam.log. It must contain no Intro.wld open failure and no 'gfx_iRefreshRate is not declared'.
titles.verifier_notes: The compat DB note for .240 dated 08-31 11:43 ('campaign loads 1_0_InTheLastEpisode') predates the truncating writer reaching that box. That box's current log shows the Intro.wld failure. The DB row for .246 (now .195) says 'd3d', but the .195 log shows OpenGL. The sam_iDriver=1 in .195's PersistentSymbols.ini is an undeclared identifier in TSE (log: PersistentSymbols.ini(4)).

titles.title: Shogo
titles.engine: LithTech 1.0 (Monolith, Shogo: Mobile Armor Division), 2.2-patch era. Client.exe is 582,144 B, linked 1999-03-05. d3d.ren is 305,152 B, linked 1999-03-09 (md5 072bc3706128209103281d6d5c53d724), and soft.ren is also present. CShell.dll v3 was carved from SHOGOP3.REZ at offset 0x2bca8: 525,824 B, linked 1999-03-09, md5 eb0286632a78bd488bd0f41f37114c4d. The launcher Shogo.exe was linked 1999-02-24.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 fullscreen at 16 bpp. Both launchers call FLEETRES.BAT and then "-setline autoexec.cfg screenwidth `screenwidth` `%FR_W%`" plus the matching screenheight line: 'Play Shogo - direct engine.bat', the primary shortcut that runs Client.exe with the -rez chain, and 'Play Shogo.bat', the fallback. GAMERES has mirror SETLINE rules. FLEETRES strips quotes when it matches the key. The deployed autoexec.cfg on .123, .145, .195 and .240 reads "screenwidth" "1920", "screenheight" "1080", "screendepth" "16" and "RenderDll" "d3d.ren"; the library copy still says 640/480. PER-TITLE-STATUS records a measurement on .145: window class LithTech at 1920x1080, rendering. The mechanism is present and correct for the direct-engine shortcut. For the fallback shortcut, Shogo.exe reads autoexec.cfg (0x405ec0) and appends its own ' ++screenwidth %i ++screenheight %i ++screendepth %i' from the mode it has selected (0x403769). Whether it picks up 1920x1080 is unverified.
titles.menu_source: Enumerated from the driver, 16 bpp only. d3d.ren exports GetSupportedModes, which calls IDirectDraw2::EnumDisplayModes(0,NULL,NULL,cb). Its callback at 0x1000fa10 keeps every mode whose DDSURFACEDESC dwRGBBitCount (+0x54) equals 16. There is no width, height or refresh filter; it stores w at +0x194, h at +0x198 and bpp at +0x19c. CShell.dll v3 at 0x10003470, called lazily from the display menu at 0x10003426, groups ClientDE::GetRenderModes() by renderer DLL and device and formats each entry with '%d x %d' (string at 0x1006f0d4), again with no size filter. The in-game DISPLAY OPTIONS / DISPLAY MODE menu (UTF-16 strings in SHOGOP3.REZ) therefore lists every 16-bpp mode the driver offers. That includes 1920 x 1080 wherever the driver offers a 16-bpp 1080p mode; the .145 measurement at 1920x1080 with screendepth 16 shows one exists there. The vendor launcher's own display dialog in Shogo.exe ('%i x %i x %i') uses the same GetSupportedModes call.
titles.evidence: All paths below are under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/. static-shogo-modes.txt holds the d3d.ren exports, the callback disassembly (cmp dword ptr [ebp+0x54],0x10), the CShell list builder, the UTF-16 strings 'DISPLAY OPTIONS', 'DISPLAY MODE' and 'resolution', and the staged autoexec video lines. {123,145,195,240}/Shogo__autoexec.cfg lines 43-44 read 1080/1920. {box}/gameres.json shows the driver lists including 1920x1080@60, without bpp. launch.txt names 'Play Shogo - direct engine.bat' as the primary shortcut.
titles.fix_risk: n/a. Caveats: the list is 16 bpp only. The 16-bpp 1080p mode is proven only on .145, and whether Win7 on .195 enumerates 16-bpp modes is unverified. CShell stores 12 resolution slots per device inline (0x1cc-byte device records), and a longer list spills into unused device slots. The list is in reverse enumeration order, so the largest modes, including 1920x1080, come first. docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md says the client menu renders intermittently.
titles.hw_check: On .145 (XP), launch with EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Shogo" "Play Shogo - direct engine.bat". Wait for the intro and the main menu, then SCREENSHOT 0. Capture worked on .145 per PER-TITLE-STATUS; the DB records a black capture on .240. Use the KEYBOARD: UIKEY DOWN/UP/RETURN to reach OPTIONS > DISPLAY, then step the display mode list with LEFT/RIGHT or UP/DOWN and screenshot each step. Pass: '1920 x 1080' is present and is the current mode. The mouse cannot be used: docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md:403 records that Shogo's menus follow relative mouse movement, which UICLICK cannot drive. Keyboard navigation is expected to work but has not yet been exercised through the agent. Close the game with taskkill /f /im "Client.exe".

titles.title: Turok2
titles.engine: Acclaim/Iguana Turok 2 engine, 1998 English retail. The DirectX 6 Direct3D renderer is Video_D3D.dll (278,528 B, linked 1999-02-02, md5 b3919d01613a234a485fef78c2999fc6); Video_3DFx.dll is the Glide renderer. Single player is Turok2English.exe (linked 1999-01-17), which checks for the Turok 2 CD; no image of that CD exists on the share. Multiplayer is Turok2MPEnglish.exe (linked 1999-02-02), which has no CD check.
titles.launch_sets: 1024x768 fullscreen, 32-bit: the largest 4:3 entry in its list that does not exceed FR_W43=1280 (1280x960 on these panels). All three launchers call FLEETRES.BAT, compute T2SEL (640, 800 or 1024 via GEQ tests) and use -setline on the six Data\config.ned booleans to set 1024^x^768 to 1. PER-TITLE-STATUS verified that on .145. The launcher is correct, but the GAMERES rule is WRONG on the 1080p boxes. gameres.h uses %SEL43:WxH%, an exact match against the 4:3 target 1280x960, which Turok's list does not contain. Every GAMESYNC or GAMERES pass therefore writes ALL SIX mode booleans to 0. The deployed Data\config.ned on all four LCD boxes shows exactly that: every '...x^... 0'. The launcher sets 1024 back to 1 at each start and the next pass zeroes it again, so the value never settles and breaks the '0 value(s) changed' contract. A start that bypasses the launcher gets no mode at all, because the width and height globals stay 0. The single-player shortcut 'Turok 2 - Seeds of Evil.lnk' is on all four desktops but cannot start without the missing CD.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded 6-entry list compiled into Video_D3D.dll. The option records sit at 0x1001b030 with stride 0x44 and are named '320 x 240', '512 x 384', '640 x 480', '800 x 600', '1024 x 768' and '1280 x 1024'. The DirectDraw mode callback at 0x1000223a marks a record available only on an exact match of 320x240, 512x384, 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768 or 1280x1024 (cmp against 0x140/0xf0 ... 0x500/0x400). The 'Direct3D Properties' dialog (RT_DIALOG 102, Resolution combobox id 0x3f8) is filled at 0x10001750 from those records only. In-game, OPTIONS > VIDEO opens the exe's 'Video' dialog (RT_DIALOG 131, a driver list), and its Properties button opens that dialog. On these LCDs the highest entry listed is 1280 x 1024, a 5:4 mode the launcher deliberately never selects. There is no custom resolution.
titles.evidence: All paths below are under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/. static-turok2-video_d3d.txt holds the option records, the callback compares, the mode-set immediates and the combobox fill. {123,145,195,240}/Turok2__Data_config.ned show every mode at 0; the library copy at /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Turok2/Data/config.ned has 800^x^600 set to 1. The Turok2 rules are in agent/shared/gameres.h, and tests/native/test_gameres.c:301-306 asserts that SEL43:1024x768 expands to '0' on a 1080p panel. 'Play Turok 2.bat' carries the T2SEL ladder. Data/single.mnu and multi.mnu both contain 'VIDEO / View/change video setup'.
titles.fix: (1) Make the GAMERES rule mirror the launcher: select the largest Turok entry that fits inside the 4:3 target, which is 1024x768 when W43 is 1280x960. That needs a new token, for example %SELFIT43:1024x768% with a ladder, plus updates to test_gameres.c and test_gameres_mirror.py. Without it GAMESYNC keeps zeroing the mode on every 1080p box. (2) The only way to get 1920x1080 in-game is a code patch of Video_D3D.dll that repurposes the unused 5:4 record. Change the label at file offset 0x1b3a4 from '1280 x 1024' to '1920 x 1080' (same 11 bytes); that also renames the config.ned key to 1920^x^1080. Change the width immediate in the enumeration check at file offset 0x22c5 from 0x500 to 0x780, and the width immediate in the mode set at 0x16e4 from 0x500 to 0x780. The two heights reuse a register holding 0x400: 'cmp [esi+8],ecx' at 0x22cb, and 'mov [0x1001fd94],eax' at 0x16e8, where eax is also the 1024x768 width. Each therefore needs a jump to a code cave; .text has about 0xF00 bytes of slack. The launcher, stage-fleetres and gameres keys must then follow the new name. Otherwise no fix is possible: the list is compiled in, and the share has no official patch or community fix for the 1998 PC release. The share only has Turok 2 demos, Turok 1 GOG/Remastered, and dgVoodoo2_87. dgVoodoo only forces a resolution from outside the game on Win7+ with D3D11, adds no in-game option, and does not run on the XP boxes.
titles.fix_source: (1) Repo: agent/shared/gameres.h, tests/native/test_gameres.c and tests/python/test_gameres_mirror.py. (2) An in-tree binary edit of /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Turok2/Video_D3D.dll; nothing to download.
titles.fix_risk: (1) Low: it is agent-side logic, but it needs an agent release. (2) High: a hand-made code patch of a 1998 DirectX 6 renderer. The projection is probably fixed at 4:3, so the picture would stretch, and the 2D menus and HUD at 1920 wide are untested. Video_3DFx.dll is untouched, and multiplayer is unaffected because the render DLL only runs on the client. The edit keeps the file size, so publish through gvfs.
titles.hw_check: On .145 (XP), launch with EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Turok2" "Play Turok 2 - Multiplayer.bat"; the single-player exe cannot pass its CD check. In the in-game menu (keyboard arrows and Enter) go to OPTIONS > VIDEO. That opens Win32 dialogs: 'Video', then Properties, then 'Direct3D Properties'. They are standard dialogs, so Tab, Alt+Down and the arrow keys work, absolute UICLICK works, and GDI captures them. Open the Resolution combobox and take a SCREENSHOT. Expected: 640 x 480 / 800 x 600 / 1024 x 768 / 1280 x 1024 only, with no 1920 x 1080. Press Cancel. Also DOWNLOAD C:\Games\Turok2\Data\config.ned before the launch (all 0 after GAMERES) and after it (1024^x^768 1) to show the churn.
titles.verifier_notes: The compat DB 'perbox' rows from 2026-08-31 10:50-10:52 claim 'Play Turok 2.bat verified 1920x1080' on .123, .240 and .246. That cannot be true: the engine has no 1920x1080 mode, and that shortcut needs a CD that does not exist. They appear to have recorded the desktop mode as the game's.

titles.title: HiddenAndDangerous
titles.engine: Illusion Softworks / Lonely Cat Games engine, Hidden & Dangerous Deluxe v1.50 (the 2003 freeware re-release). Bin\HDE.exe is 1,073,197 B, linked 2003-10-03. igraph2.dll (created through IGraphCreate) is the Direct3D 8 layer, next to i3d2.dll. A separate vendor configuration tool, Bin\IConfig.exe, was linked 2003-09-29.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080 fullscreen, 32-bit. The engine reads its mode only from HKLM\Software\Lonely Cat Games\Hidden and Dangerous Deluxe\Config. All three launchers write 'Display width', 'Display height', 'Display bitdepth' and 'Fullscreen' there with FLEETRES -reg, overriding the 800x600 that install.reg sets. GAMERES REG rules rewrite the same values at sync, after gs_merge_reg. REGREAD on .123, .145, .195 and .240 returns Fullscreen=1, Display width=1920, Display height=1080 and Display bitdepth=32. PER-TITLE-STATUS records a measurement on .145: IGraph_Window at 1920x1080, true 16:9, rendering. Present and correct.
titles.menu_source: Enumerated from the driver. The in-game menu is Options > Video; manual p.17 describes it as 'Choosing the screen resolution, full-screen or windowed option ... APPLY CHANGES'. HDE.exe builds it in mc_VideoConfigCallback at 0x462450. That symbol comes from the MSVC linker map embedded in Data\data.dta, and the function prologue at that address matches the staged build. The function loops over IGraph::NumDisplayModes (vtable +0xdc) and GetDisplayMode (+0xe0). In igraph2.dll, GetDisplayMode (0x10007360) passes IDirect3D8::EnumAdapterModes through unfiltered. The menu keeps modes with w>=512 (0x200) and h>=384 (0x180), removes duplicates keyed on (h<<16|w), sorts by w*h (comparator at 0x462f30) and formats each as '%i x %i'. There is no upper bound, so 1920 x 1080 is listed, last. IConfig.exe's Resolution combobox is also filled from the driver: D3D8 modes of at least 512x384 and 16 bpp, duplicates removed.
titles.evidence: All paths below are under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/. static-hd-videomenu.txt holds the HDE.exe loop, the igraph2 pass-through, the format strings (HDE.exe file offset 0xf3e3c '%i x %i') and the manual text. {123,145,195,240}/reg-HD-config.txt hold the registry values. {box}/dirlist-HiddenAndDangerous.json shows that no LCD box has a Savegame directory, so none has a profile. README-FLEET.txt in the tree says 'STILL BLOCKED: THE GAME PROFILE - NEEDS A HUMAN ONCE'.
titles.fix: None needed for the list. The launcher rewrites the HKLM mode at every start, so an in-game APPLY lasts only one session; on these LCDs that makes no difference, since the launcher writes the same 1920x1080. Unattended use of the menu is blocked a step earlier. The first screen, 'Select game profile', needs a profile that no LCD box has. It ignores the keyboard and its cursor follows relative mouse movement.
titles.hw_check: The in-game check needs a person at .145 once, to create a profile on the 'Select game profile' screen with the mouse. Then open Options > Video and SCREENSHOT the resolution list. Expected: '1920 x 1080' at the end of the list, which is sorted by area. Do not press APPLY CHANGES. An unattended proxy reads the same D3D8 source: LAUNCH C:\Games\HiddenAndDangerous\Bin\IConfig.exe. It is a standard Win32 dialog, so the keyboard and absolute clicks work and GDI can capture it. SCREENSHOT its Resolution combobox and expect '1920 x 1080'. Leave with Cancel, because OK writes the HKLM Config key. Then REGREAD that key to confirm nothing changed.

titles.title: AliensVsPredator
titles.engine: Rebellion's Aliens versus Predator engine, Gold Edition. avp.exe is 2,169,856 B, linked 2000-03-22, md5 91bb8e752f42d35f594fc06feabd49cf. It is a Watcom build using DirectDraw 6 and Direct3D.
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 at 16 bpp, and the game hangs before its menu. The library still deploys the tree, although PER-TITLE-STATUS lists it as 'not staged, CLOSED as BLOCKED'. launch.txt reads 'avp.exe<TAB>Aliens vs Predator<TAB>avp.exe', and 'Aliens vs Predator.lnk' is on all four LCD desktops. There is no Play*.bat, no FLEETRES and no GAMERES rule. No LCD box has an AvP_Video.cfg, so avp.exe uses its built-in default of 640x480x16 (code at 0x5598f8 compares 0x280, 0x1e0 and 0x10); the DB records 'd3d 640x480'. On .123, .145, .195 and .240 the last run's LOGFILE.TXT (dated 2026-08-29 and 2026-08-31) ends with 'CL_LoadImageOnce(): ... Menus\IntroFont.rim ... ERROR: file not found', then 'AwCreateGraphic(): ERROR: No data medium is specified', then 'ASSERTION FAILED! Expression: pSurface File: ..\3dc\win95\alt_tab.cpp Line: 198'. None of those logs contains a 'Loaded FastFile' line. The result is a hung, black, exclusive 640x480 screen, and that hang is what the DB's 'runs' rows recorded.
titles.menu_source: By the code, the list comes from the driver, but no one has ever seen it. The DirectDraw EnumDisplayModes callback at 0x559344 keeps modes with bpp>8, w>=512 and h>=384 whose depth the D3D device caps allow (flags at [0x85c569]), and stops after 100 modes (cmp esi,0x64). The Options video list steps through (device, mode) pairs (0x559748 and 0x559798) and saves the choice to AvP_Video.cfg as 32 bytes: a 16-byte DirectDraw device GUID, a flag, then w, h and bpp. It would list 1920x1080 unless the 100-mode cap cuts the list off first. The menu has never been reached on this fleet, so the answer is unknown.
titles.evidence: All paths below are under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/ss-shogo-turok-hd-avp/. static-avp-data-check.txt shows that in the staged tree every fastfile/Tex1-58.FFL begins 9cc8f4e8 instead of 'RFFL', ffinfo.txt begins c8185818, and avp_huds/alien.rif begins 9cccc4cc. The same files from Freeware & Open Source/Classic Freeware/AvP_1999_Disc1.iso are plain text: 'RFFL', 'Graphics\Common;' and 'REBCRIF1'. The same file compares the tree with the Gold-install MD5 list in github.com/atsb/NakedAVP (a web source): of 201 files, 56 match (all Snd*.FFL, common.ffl, the *.dat files and language.txt) and 145 differ (every Tex*.FFL, ffinfo.txt, and every avp_huds and avp_rifs .rif). avp.exe imports no drive or volume APIs, only mciSendCommandA, so this is not a CD-keyed check. The per-box logs are {123,145,195,240}/AliensVsPredator__LOGFILE.TXT.
titles.fix: No resolution fix is possible until the title starts. The root-cause lead is unverified. README-FLEET says the tree is a byte copy of the disc payload, yet the known-good installed Gold data differs in exactly the graphics and level files, so the retail installer probably transforms them. Re-capture the tree by running the Gold installer in the build VM, as CLAUDE.md requires, from 'Games/Windows XP/Aliens vs Predator Gold (1999) - Disc 1.zip', then test again. Until then, either withdraw launch.txt and purge the .lnk and the tree from the boxes (GAMESYNC never deletes), or record plainly that every box carries a shortcut that hangs. Once the game runs, 1080p per box can come from a launcher that writes AvP_Video.cfg (a zero or real device GUID plus 1920/1080/32), or from the in-game Options > Video list.
titles.fix_source: The installer's output would be needed, and no resolution payload exists yet. The disc images are already on the share: /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games/Windows XP/Aliens vs Predator Gold (1999) - Disc 1.zip holds a MODE2/2352 .bin/.cue, and the 1999 disc is /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games/Freeware & Open Source/Classic Freeware/AvP_1999_Disc1.iso.
titles.fix_risk: Re-staging is a large change and belongs in the build VM, not on a fleet box. The 1999 plaintext data cannot simply be mixed with the Gold exe and levels. How this engine handles a 16:9 aspect has not been evaluated.
titles.hw_check: First prove it starts. On .145, EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\AliensVsPredator" "avp.exe", wait 30 s, taskkill /f /im "avp.exe", then DOWNLOAD C:\Games\AliensVsPredator\LOGFILE.TXT. It passes only with 'Loaded FastFile:' lines and no 'ASSERTION FAILED'. Only after that check Options > Video. docs/lan-multiplayer-status.md:403 lists AvP among the relative-mouse menus, so drive it with the keyboard. GDI SCREENSHOT is black for AvP even on XP (measured on .133), so verify the result through LOGFILE, DISPLAYCFG get after applying 1920x1080, or a person at the screen.
titles.verifier_notes: PER-TITLE-STATUS says 'not staged', but the library deploys the title to every box, so that register row is wrong about the library. The compat DB rows 'runs, d3d 640x480' come from mode-change and live-process evidence that also fits the observed assertion hang. Its title note 'graphics fastfile content absent from every distribution' is likewise not what the files show: the graphics fastfiles are present but obfuscated.
